summary: A QR code generator you host: live preview, colours, dot styles and a centre logo, PNG and SVG export, plus dynamic codes on your own domain that redirect through /r/:slug so a printed code can be repointed later, with per-code scan counts. The domain is the one thing you must keep forever.

stack.why: handles dots, corners and logos; pinned and served by you, not a CDN
a redirect is one lookup and a 302
codes and scans in one file

stack.choice: A VPS behind Caddy on a domain you will keep
stack.why: a printed code outlives the tool that made it

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A phone with a camera
prerequisites.why: Every check in Phases 1 to 3 is scanning the code with a real camera. Emulators do not count.
prerequisites.get: Any modern phone; the stock camera app scans QR codes.

prerequisites.name: A square logo file (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 3 tests the centre-logo feature; a real logo shows whether it still scans.
prerequisites.get: Your logo as PNG or SVG, at least 256x256, ideally with transparent background.

prerequisites.name: A domain you will keep for years
prerequisites.why: Dynamic codes redirect through your domain. If the domain lapses, every printed code becomes dead paper. Do not use a domain you might drop.
prerequisites.get: Register a short one at Porkbun or Cloudflare Registrar and turn on auto-renew. A subdomain of a domain you already keep is fine.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: DATABASE_PATH
env.where: SQLite file for codes and scans.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base of the redirect domain. Baked into every dynamic code.

env.name: FALLBACK_URL
env.where: Where a deactivated or unknown code lands. A dead printed code should explain itself.

env.name: IP_SALT
env.where: openssl rand -hex 32, once. For hashing scanner IPs.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Static generator
phases.goal: Type text, see a code, scan it.

steps.do: Create the project and vendor qr-code-styling
steps.detail: Install the pinned version and copy its browser bundle into public/vendor so nothing loads from a CDN at runtime.
commands: mkdir qr && cd qr && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Build the page: a text field and a live preview
steps.detail: new QRCodeStyling({ width: 300, height: 300, type: 'canvas', data }) then .append(container). Re-render on input with a 150 ms debounce.

check: Typing a URL produces a code a phone camera resolves to exactly that URL
Clearing the field leaves no broken canvas behind

phases.title: Customization
phases.goal: Colours and styles that update live, with a warning when the result would not scan.

steps.do: Add colour, dot style, corner style and margin controls
steps.detail: dotsOptions.color and type (square, rounded, classy), cornersSquareOptions, backgroundOptions.color, margin. Every control re-renders immediately; no Apply button.
Compute the contrast ratio between foreground and background; below roughly 3:1 show a warning while still rendering. A beautiful unscannable code is the failure users ship.

check: Every control visibly changes the preview
A low-contrast pair shows the warning and the code still renders
A rounded-dots code still scans

phases.title: Centre logo
phases.goal: A logo in the middle that does not break scanning.

steps.do: Wire an image upload to image and imageOptions
steps.detail: imageSize around 0.3, margin, hideBackgroundDots true. Read the file locally with FileReader; nothing is uploaded.

steps.do: Raise error correction to H whenever a logo is present
steps.detail: qrOptions.errorCorrectionLevel = 'H' with a logo, back to M without. Cap the logo at roughly a quarter of the code.

check: A code with a logo at maximum size scans from 30 cm
Removing the logo restores the previous error-correction level

phases.title: Export
phases.goal: PNG and SVG that reopen correctly, and copy to clipboard that works in Safari too.

steps.do: Add download buttons with a size selector
steps.detail: download({ name, extension: 'png' | 'svg' }) at 512, 1024 or 2048 by re-instantiating at that size.

Always pass a Promise resolving to a Blob into ClipboardItem: Safari requires the promise form and Chromium accepts it, so one code path works everywhere. Call navigator.clipboard.write inside the click handler or the user gesture is lost.

check: PNG and SVG both download and reopen correctly
The 2048px export is sharp
Copy pastes an image in both Safari and a Chromium browser

phases.title: Dynamic codes
phases.goal: Codes that point at /r/:slug so the target can change after printing.

steps.do: Create the codes table and the server
steps.detail: codes (id, slug unique, target_url, label, created_at, updated_at, active). Slugs 6+ characters from an alphabet without 0/O/1/l/I, CSPRNG-generated, or custom.
302 to target_url. Unknown or inactive slugs redirect to FALLBACK_URL rather than 404ing.

steps.do: Build /admin behind basic auth with CRUD
steps.detail: Editing a target must never change the slug. Deactivating keeps the row. Each row shows its code image and a download button.

check: A printed code for /r/:slug scans, then after editing the target scans to the new destination with no regeneration
A deactivated code lands on the fallback page
Creating a slug named admin or r is refused
traps: A slug is permanent. Rewriting one invalidates every printed code that uses it, which is the one unrecoverable mistake this tool can make.

phases.title: Scan analytics
phases.goal: Counts you can explain, written after the redirect.

steps.do: Log scans after issuing the redirect
steps.detail: scans (id, code_id, scanned_at, referer, user_agent_class, ip_hash). Never before the 302.

steps.do: Bucket bots and show totals plus a 30-day sparkline per code
steps.detail: Link scanners and chat previewers inflate counts otherwise.

check: A scan increments the count
A Slack link preview is bucketed as bot and excluded
The redirect still works with the database stopped

phases.title: Deploy
phases.goal: Live on the domain you will keep, backed up, documented.

steps.do: Add /healthz, systemd, Caddy and a nightly backup
Turn on domain auto-renew and write the README
steps.detail: README: the domain-is-forever warning stated once plainly, which error-correction level is used and why it changes with a logo, and when to use static instead of dynamic.

check: A reader goes from clone to a working dynamic code on their own domain using only the README
Auto-renew is confirmed on at the registrar

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the redirect is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A QR service you could run for a small business: static codes for free, dynamic codes on a domain with auto-renew and backups, and scan counts that separate people from bots.

architecture.owns: the browser page and vendored library
architecture.swap: Any renderer producing the same PNG/SVG; the server does not know about it
A serverless function reading the same table
Drop or replace without touching redirects
Any UI; slugs are the contract

operations.backup: SQLite .backup nightly. The codes table is the asset: without it every printed code is dead.
operations.restore: Copy back and start; verify one known slug redirects correctly.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz and on one known /r/ slug from an external checker, since a dead redirect is invisible from inside.
operations.incident: If the domain expires, renew immediately: registrars hold a grace period. If the database is lost without backup, printed codes cannot be recovered; this is why backups are not optional.

releaseGate: Domain auto-renew on, with a calendar reminder a month before expiry
One restore drill performed and dated
External check on a live /r/ slug passing

notIncluded: Hosted redirects on someone else's short domain. Yours must be a domain you will keep.
Their scan-analytics product and bulk generation UI.
after: Bulk creation from a CSV with a ZIP of PNGs
Per-code UTM parameters appended on redirect
